slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client who asks the nurse to witness an advance directive. Which of the following actions should the nurse to implement?
text: The nurse is caring for a client who asks the nurse to witness an advance directive. Which of the following actions should the nurse to implement?
Agree to sign the document as a witness.
Notify the PHCP of the client's request.
Help the client locate an unrelated third party.

slides.title: Decline the clients request politely. Does not help the client.
text: Decline the clients request politely. Does not help the client.
Agree to sign the document as a witness.  Illegal.
Notify the PHCP of the client's request. Not the best intervention.
Help the client locate an unrelated third party. Correct. Two unrelated people witness the signature and sign the document, nurse cannot sign or family member. It's a conflict of interest.

slides.title: 16-year-old married client scheduled for a C-Section.
text: 16-year-old married client scheduled for a C-Section.
Yes, an emancipated minor because is married under age 18.
59-year-old client who speaks Spanish only. NO, this client
30-year-old client who just received amoxicillin. Yes, this is an antibiotic and will not affect the client's ability to legally sign a document.
88-year-old client who is blind but alert and oriented. Yes, this client can still
sign since the disability does not affect comprehension.
E.  17-year-old client who needs emergency appendectomy. No, a minor.

slides.title: Which of the following activities should the nurse delegate to the unlicensed assistant personnel(UAP)? Select all that apply.

Take vital signs on a new admission.

Demonstrate how to use an incentive spirometry.

slides.title: Take vital signs on a new admission. No, only RNs assess new admissions.
text: Take vital signs on a new admission. No, only RNs assess new admissions.
Assist with the narcotic count. No, only nurse can do this.
Check the crash cart for necessary supplies. No, only nurse can do this.
Administer a tap water enema. Yes, there are no medications or electrolytes in the enema.
Obtain client finger sticks on diabetic clients. Yes, this is in their scope of practice.
Demonstrate how to use an incentive spirometry. No, they can not teach.

slides.title: Which of the following clinical situations should be viewed as an assault?
text: Which of the following clinical situations should be viewed as an assault?
The nurse threatens to apply restraints to a client who is exhibiting aggressive behavior.
The client requests a medical discharge, but the nurse physically forces the client to stay.
The charge nurse sends an email to a staff member which includes a poor performance evaluation about another person.
The nurse overhears the primary health care provider making derogatory remarks to the client about the nurse's level of competency.

slides.title: The nurse threatens to apply restraints to a client who is exhibiting aggressive behavior. Yes, assault is a threat to harm.
text: The nurse threatens to apply restraints to a client who is exhibiting aggressive behavior. Yes, assault is a threat to harm.
The client requests a medical discharge, but the nurse physically forces the client to stay. No, this would be battery.
The charge nurse sends an email to a staff member which includes a poor performance evaluation about another person. No, this would be inappropriate and violate the staff members rights.
The nurse overhears the primary health care provider making derogatory remarks to the client about the nurse's level of competency. No, this would be defamation.

slides.title: Which of the following actions by the nurse demonstrate ethical practice? Select all that apply
text: Which of the following actions by the nurse demonstrate ethical practice? Select all that apply
Notifies PHCP about a client refusing dialysis and wants to stop.
Educates client about use and benefits of incentive spirometry when refusing to use device.
Refuses to stay overnight on a mandated shift due to fatigue, leaves at the end of current scheduled shift.
Confronts a coworker who took narcotics out of a client's medication bin for personal use and takes no further action.
Asks a client to “take a walk down the hall so their roommate can speak with the PHCP privately about their biopsy results.”
Tells a client they will find out an answer for them.

slides.title: Notifies PHCP about a client refusing dialysis and wants to stop. Yes.
text: Notifies PHCP about a client refusing dialysis and wants to stop. Yes.
Educates client about use and benefits of incentive spirometry when refusing to use device. Yes.

Refuses to stay overnight on a mandated shift due to fatigue, leaves at the end of scheduled current shift.  Nurse can not leave clients without another nurse to care for them, client abandonment.  No!
Confronts a coworker who took narcotics out of a client's medication bin for personal use and takes no further action. Nurse did not ethically report this matter to the chain of command, NO!
Asks a client to “take a walk down the hall with me so your roommate can speak with the PHCP privately about their biopsy results.”  Nurse must not give information about other clients, NO!
Tells a client they will find out an answer for them. Yes.

slides.title: Ethical Practice
text: Practices with compassion and respect for the inherent dignity, worth, and unique attributes of every person
Primary commitment is to the client, whether an individual, family, group, community, or population
Promotes, advocates for, and protects the rights, health, and safety of the client
Authority, accountability, and responsibility for nursing practice; makes decisions; and acts consistent with the obligation to promote health and to provide optimal care

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a multiple gunshot victim. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to properly secure and handle legal evidence? Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is caring for a multiple gunshot victim. Which of the following actions should the nurse take to properly secure and handle legal evidence? Select all that apply.
Place bags on the hands and feet.
Give clothing and wallet to the family.
Cut clothing along the seams, avoiding bullet holes.
Collect all personal items, including items from clothing pockets.
Place wet clothing and personal belongings in a labeled, sealed plastic bag.
Do not allow family members, significant others, or friends to be alone with the client.

slides.title: Place paper bags on the hands and feet. Yes, need to preserve evidence.
text: Place paper bags on the hands and feet. Yes, need to preserve evidence.
Give clothing and wallet to the family. No, this might be needed for evidence in future.
Cut clothing along the seams, avoiding bullet holes. Yes, forensics will need to test the bullet hole areas.
Collect all personal items, including items from clothing pockets. Yes, it will all need listed for potential evidence.
Place wet clothing and personal belongings in a labeled, sealed plastic bag. No, this could harm the evidence if placed with wet items. They should be placed separately, labeled, and sealed.
Do not allow family members, significant others, or friends to be alone with the client. Yes, they could tamper with evidence.

slides.title: The nurse is discussing living wills with a client. The client asks the nurse if a living will, prepared 3 years ago, remains in effect. Which response should the nurse provide to the client?
text: The nurse is discussing living wills with a client. The client asks the nurse if a living will, prepared 3 years ago, remains in effect. Which response should the nurse provide to the client?
“You need to speak to an attorney.”
“I will call someone to answer your question.”
It is recommended to review them yearly and update with your health care provider.”

slides.title: “Yes, a living will never expire.” Not the best answer.
text: “Yes, a living will never expire.” Not the best answer.
“You need to speak to an attorney.”  An attorney does not have to complete an advance directive.
“I will call someone to answer your question.”  This does not provide the client with help.
“It is recommended to review them yearly and update with your health care provider.”  Yes, it is recommended to review them yearly and update with the health care provider.
